subject: Commit reconciliation: make-goods, proration, and quarterly cadence
messages:
From: Claire Liu <claire.liu@bluewave.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@bluewave.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit reconciliation & make-goods — questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're close to finalizing internal budget approval but have a few outstanding questions about how Redwood handles commit reconciliation and make-goods for the hosted API:

- If we commit to a 12M-token tier for Q4 and under-consume, how is that shortfall handled operationally? Credit on next invoice, or a separate adjustment?
- Do you run reconciliation quarterly or annually by default? Can we opt for monthly true-ups?
- If we increase commit mid-quarter, how is proration calculated? Conversely, if we decrease the commit, when does it take effect?
- Any limits on converting unused hosted commit to credits toward Dedicated or Marketplace purchases?

Procurement would like an example calculation (pro-forma) and a short playbook we can include in the SOW addendum. Can you share internal guidance and the typical cadence Redwood follows?

Thanks,
Claire Liu
Head of Platform Partnerships
BlueWave Analytics

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Claire Liu <claire.liu@bluewave.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit reconciliation & make-goods — questions

Claire, thanks for the clear list — good questions. Below is a concise playbook + how we typically operate; attaching our pricing matrix and a pro-forma example so your procurement team can model scenarios.

Summary (short):
- Reconcile cadence: Quarterly by default (end of quarter true-up). We can offer monthly reporting and monthly true-ups for customers with complex cashflow needs, but that adds operational overhead.
- Shortfalls (under-consumption): Standard approach is to credit the customer's account for the shortfall at the quarterly true-up. Credits appear on the next invoice as an account-level credit memo. Exception: for negotiated deals we can invoice the shortfall instead (customer preference), or convert to a make-good (one-time token grant) per SOW.
- Over-usage: Overages are billed at the overage per-token rate in the pricing matrix; we can cap overage exposure with pre-agreed thresholds.
- Proration: Increases take effect immediately and prorate for the remaining days in the billing period. Reductions take effect at the next quarter boundary unless otherwise negotiated in the SOW (to avoid churn and capacity accounting issues).
- Conversion to Dedicated credits: Possible, but must be specified in the SOW. Typically we allow a partial conversion (e.g., up to 50% of unused hosted commit) and credit it toward a Dedicated commitment within 90 days.

I'll summarize this in a short SOW addendum draft and propose a sample cadence: monthly usage reporting -> quarterly reconciliation -> credit issuance within 30 days of reconciliation.

Attached: redwood-pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx, pro-forma-trueup-example.xlsx

Next step: If that structure works for BlueWave, I can circulate a 1-page addendum and a worked example for your legal/procurement.

— Rafael Mendes
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Claire Liu <claire.liu@bluewave.ai>, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit reconciliation & make-goods — questions

Looping in a quick policy note from the sales ops perspective so expectations are clear:

- Standard discount bands are applied to committed tiers; make-goods/credits are separate from discounts and do not change historical discounting.
- Recommended playbook we use for commercial deals:
  1) Quarterly reconciliation window: 0–30 days after quarter close we validate usage.
  2) If shortfall <= 15% of committed tokens for the quarter: apply account credit equal to shortfall * committed effective per-token price.
  3) If shortfall > 15% and <= 35%: offer make-good token grant up to the shortfall OR convert to a one-time credit at the customer’s choice.
  4) If shortfall > 35%: trigger Commercial Review — we typically reserve the right to renegotiate commit bands for future quarters and may require an amendment.

- Cap on credits: generally we cap total annual credits to 25% of annual committed spend unless pre-approved by finance.

Attached is a pro-forma with example math (pro-forma-trueup-example.xlsx). Happy to run BlueWave's numbers if you share expected monthly token volumes.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Claire Liu <claire.liu@bluewave.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@bluewave.ai, Samir Raj <samir.raj@bluewave.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit reconciliation & make-goods — questions

Thanks Rafael and Ben — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement:

- We do prefer invoice-level adjustments rather than account credits for auditability; is that acceptable or is credit memos the only supported path?
- If we increase commit mid-quarter, will you prorate at token-level (days remaining * daily capacity) or simply apply a flat percentage based on days remaining? We want deterministic math for our treasury team.
- Regarding conversions to Dedicated credits: procurement needs to understand the conversion rate (hosted token units -> Dedicated USD credit) and any blackout windows when conversion is disallowed.

Also: we may ask for monthly true-ups in the SOW so we can limit budget drift. There is some flexibility if the operational cost is reasonable.

Could you circulate the SOW addendum and a one-page table showing "Scenario / Result / Timing" so our legal can sign quickly?

Best,
Claire

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Claire Liu <claire.liu@bluewave.ai>, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit reconciliation & make-goods — questions

Claire — quick clarifications from the commercial policy side to address procurement's bullets:

- Invoice adjustments vs account credit: Finance prefers issuing a credit memo applied to the next invoice (cleaner for our accounting), but we can generate a standalone invoice-level negative adjustment if your auditors require it. We'll note whichever approach in the SOW.

- Proration math: we prorate to token-level using the precise daily allocation. Example: if you add 3M tokens on day 10 of a 90-day quarter, new daily allocation applies from day 10 forward; we calculate remaining-day tokens precisely. We'll include the formula in the addendum so it's deterministic.

- Conversion to Dedicated: conversion is allowed up to 50% of the unused hosted commit within 90 days post-reconciliation; conversion is by dollar-equivalent at the effective per-token rate in the pricing matrix. Blackout windows: conversions cannot be applied during active Dedicated renewal negotiations that were signed in the prior 60 days.

Action items I will take:
- Draft 1-page SOW addendum with scenario table + deterministic formulas (proration)
- Share the DocuSign link for an amendment template we use for midterm commit changes
- Provide a worked example using your expected monthly volumes (we can run it together)

CC: Ben — please note the credit cap guidance above (25% annual) for this account.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Strategy Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Claire Liu <claire.liu@bluewave.ai>, procurement@bluewave.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit reconciliation & make-goods — questions

Claire — thanks for the back-and-forth. Quick summary and proposed next steps so everything is explicit for legal/procurement:

Agreed commercial framework:
- Reconciliation cadence: Quarterly true-up (default). Monthly true-ups available if requested in SOW (we'll include an ops fee).
- Under-consumption: Default is credit memo applied to next invoice; invoice-level negative adjustment available on request for audit reasons.
- Shortfall thresholds: <=15% credit; 15–35% make-good token grant or credit; >35% triggers commercial review. Cap on credits = 25% annual committed spend unless finance pre-approves.
- Proration: token-level, day-accurate proration for increases; reductions effective next quarter unless SOW states otherwise.
- Conversion to Dedicated: up to 50% of unused hosted commit, dollar-equivalent at effective per-token rate, within 90 days post-reconciliation. Blackout windows apply.

Next steps:
1) Vanessa to circulate 1-page SOW addendum + deterministic formula table (ETA: EOD Friday).
2) I will attach the SOW addendum to a DocuSign envelope for BlueWave review once we have the table.
3) If BlueWave confirms monthly volumes, Ben will run the pro-forma numbers and we will share a worked spreadsheet.

Can you confirm whether BlueWave prefers (A) credit memo on the account, or (B) invoice-level negative adjustment for auditability? Also, confirm if you want monthly true-ups (we'll draft the ops fee language).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this for Q4.
